model_claims.text: After a partial read via a bounded read() or read1(), stream() continues to work correctly, preserving chunked streaming.
model_claims.source_quote: Preserve chunked streaming after a partial read

model_claims.text: A bounded read() or read1() advances the HTTP/1.1 chunk parser, and a subsequent stream() starts parsing again at that offset and may treat the rest of the chunk or its trailing CRLF as an invalid chunk size.
model_claims.source_quote: A bounded `read()` or `read1()` advances the underlying HTTP/1.1 chunk parser. A subsequent `stream()` starts parsing again at that offset and can treat the rest of the chunk or its trailing CRLF as an invalid chunk size.

model_claims.text: Continuing through read() after body bytes have been read preserves the response's chunk parser state and buffered decoded data.
model_claims.source_quote: Continue through `read()` after body bytes have been read so the response keeps its chunk parser state and buffered decoded data.

model_claims.text: The tests verify correct behavior when switching from read to stream mid-chunk and exactly at a chunk boundary.
model_claims.source_quote: The tests cover switching mid-chunk and exactly at a chunk boundary.

model_claims.text: On Windows with Python 3.13, 394 tests in the response, connection pool, and socket streaming suites all pass.
model_claims.source_quote: On Windows with Python 3.13, 394 tests passed across the response, connection pool, and socket streaming suites.

model_claims.text: A loopback HTTP/1.1 server confirms that plain and gzip responses are processed completely and connections are reused correctly.
model_claims.source_quote: A loopback HTTP/1.1 server also verified complete plain and gzip responses and connection reuse.
